differences: ASSUMED, not stated by the authors, the deposit or the paper: (1) the unit of the positions is mm; (2) x runs front-back (larger towards the lips), y runs vertically (larger upwards) and z is the lateral axis. They were worked out from the data (sensor distances; the order of the sensors along x and y; the small movement along z), as described under How this file was made. The sign of z and the origin of each speaker's coordinates (which differs between speakers) are not known.

The paper says missing sensor points were filled by piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation, but 2825 sensor samples (8475 values, always all three coordinates of one sensor) are still missing in 136 of the 368 files (303 in 50 files for speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0001, 2473 in 78 files for speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0002, 26 in 5 files for speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0003, 23 in 3 files for speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0004; the longest gap is 144 samples (1.44 s) of sensor TT in recording 92 of speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0002). They are empty cells here, not filled, and processing names them for each file.

The paper gives a sampling rate of 100 Hz; the files carry a rate of their own: 100.0752-100.0838 Hz in 362 files and 97.5-98.7 Hz in 6 files (those hold fewer samples than 100 Hz times the length of their audio). time_s is the sample index divided by the file's own rate.

For speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0001 the EMA signal and the audio of a file have the same length (to 0.1 ms); for the other speakers the EMA signal is 0.06-0.96 s shorter than the audio (median 0.09 s). The audio inside the files is sampled at 22,050 Hz, where the paper says 44.1 kHz downsampled to 16 kHz; it is not part of this conversion.

The deposit's transcripts for speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0002 are named usctimit_mri_..., not usctimit_ema_..., and are byte-identical (CRC32 and size, checked against the ZIP's file directory) to the transcripts of the MRI recordings of that speaker; 1 of them has no sentence label at all. They do not fit the audio inside this speaker's EMA files: the correlation between the audio level and the speech labels is 0.36 (median over files) against 0.71-0.79 for the three other speakers; the labels fit best when shifted by 0.6 s (median over files; from -1.8 to 1.3 s, positive meaning the label lies later than the sound), so no single correction repairs them. The EMA and the audio of these files are in step with each other (see How this file was made), so it is the transcripts that do not belong to them. They are therefore not copied: no alignments and no events for this speaker.

In 272 of the 276 alignments that are kept the last interval ends 0.1-2.3 s after the end of the EMA signal (median 1.1 s), and 15 lines (all of them the first line of a file) have an end before their start. 44 gaps of more than 0.3 s (longest 4.6 s) separate consecutive lines. The alignment times are copied as the authors give them.
In 2 sentences the end given in events lies after the end of the EMA signal of the file (the alignment is longer than the signal there).
The deposit has two further transcripts and WAV files for speaker Narayanan2014_JASA_P0004 (sentences 461-470) with no EMA file; they are not converted.

The 20 Hz low-pass filter shows in the data as a steeper roll-off above 20 Hz, not as an absence of power: the median share of a sensor signal's power above 20 Hz is 0.007%, and up to 2.6% in single channels.
